title: Macaroni or Pasta Salad with Tuna and Egg

content.title: About
content.content: Macaroni or pasta salad with tuna and egg is a balanced dish that combines carbohydrates, protein, and healthy fats. It is typically made with short pasta (such as shells or penne), canned tuna, hard‑boiled eggs, vegetables, and a light dressing based on mayonnaise or yogurt.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canned tuna retains most of its omega‑3 fatty acids, which are heart‑healthy.
Eggs add not only protein but also vitamin D, a nutrient hard to obtain from plant sources.
This salad is a staple in school cafeterias and picnics because it stores well and is quick to prepare.
Different countries use different pasta shapes: Italy prefers farfalle, while Russia often uses shells or spaghetti.
The flavor improves after a few hours in the refrigerator as the ingredients meld together.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Tuna and eggs provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair and muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of omega‑3
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids from tuna support heart health and reduce inflammation.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and whole‑grain pasta supply B12, B6, and folate, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: Tuna and eggs are good sources of heme iron, which is more readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: Adds dietary fiber
items.content: Using whole‑grain pasta adds extra fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Fish or egg allergy
items.content: People allergic to fish or eggs should avoid this salad.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned tuna can be high in salt; choose low‑sodium versions if you monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Bacterial growth risk
items.content: If left at room temperature for more than 2 hours, the salad may develop harmful bacteria.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Mayonnaise‑based dressings increase calories; moderate portion sizes to manage weight.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad cold as a main dish, side, or in a lunch box. It is easy to eat with a fork or spoon. Fresh vegetables such as cucumber, tomato, or green onion can be mixed in for extra crunch and nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. If needed, add a fresh drizzle of dressing before serving to prevent the pasta from becoming soggy.
